item.title: From Starbucks to takeout, Reddit thread exposes how everyday purchases drain your budget
item.description: Reddit users in their 30s say fast food bills of $400-500 a month and daily morning coffee added up to sums that shocked them when they did the math.
item.content:encoded:
What's a quick way to blow money without realizing it?

That's a question currently generating a solid amount of attention and buzz on Reddit at the moment.

As the loyal readers know, I'm a big fan of Reddit, and just because it's Thanksgiving isn't an excuse to not dive in.

REDDIT USERS SHARE FRUGAL HABITS THEY TRIED ONCE AND REALIZED WERE 'ACTUALLY GENIUS' SAVES

That leads us to a pretty fascinating thread.

I was scrolling Reddit on Thanksgiving morning as I sipped on my black coffee when I stumbled on a thread titled, "People in your 30s, what 'small' spending habit from your 20s added up to a number that genuinely shocked you when you finally did the math?"

REDDIT USERS REVEAL 'RICH PEOPLE' HABITS THEY TRIED ONCE AND COULD NEVER GO BACK FROM

I hit click as fast as I could.

The discussion didn't disappoint. Check out some of the answers below:

AMERICANS ARE DITCHING A LONGTIME WEEKLY TRADITION AS RESTAURANT DINING HITS RECORD LOW

There is one very noticeable trend in the answers. Eating out and constantly ordering coffee is a quick way to blow a lot of money.

The crazy thing is it's an easy fix most people don't want to make. You can make lunch at your house, and it will almost certainly be better than anything you get from a fast food restaurant.

The same goes for coffee. Go to the grocery store and get as much coffee as you want for a fraction of the price. It's crazy to me that more people don't do that. I can't remember the last time I bought coffee from any place other than the grocery store. It might have been years.

The fourth episode of "Chris Harrison's: The Vow" was packed with content as Jace Cates went on another date and got a visit from his loved ones.

In the episode, titled "Mother Knows Best," Cates took Kylee out on their first solo date together, during which they went house-hunting with a real estate agent in downtown Austin.

"I think there's some women that I'm really developing strong feelings for, and I'm excited to continue this journey with them," he said. "Today I chose Kylee. Following the drama in the house, Cates was visited by Chris Harrison, who told him his parents would be visiting and would have an opportunity to meet the women, something Cates was excited about because his parents' opinion is very important to him.

"I felt like she was a little more intense. That's just a little bit of a red flag for me," his dad said. "It's OK to be strong, Lord knows your mom is, and I love her for it, but there is a difference between being strong and being a little bit rigid and combative."

item.title: Norse Atlantic airline suspends all flights, on brink of bankruptcy amid rising fuel costs
item.description: Norse Atlantic suspended all flights as its board warned it may file for bankruptcy without urgent short-term financing, leaving PIA passengers stranded.
item.content:encoded:
Norwegian airline Norse Atlantic suspended all flights Thursday as its board warned the company may imminently file for bankruptcy if it can't secure short-term financing.

"If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the Board's intention to file for bankruptcy," the company said in a statement.

The airline, which provides long-haul flights between the U.S. and Europe, said it had been discussing with investors a possible takeover that "would include a financing solution."

SHIPPING GIANT WARNS STRAIT OF HORMUZ CHAOS IS 'NEW NORMAL' AS TEHRAN SHIFTS 4M BARRELS

But, the company added, "There can be no assurance that a viable solution will be found."

Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), which contracts jets from Norse through a wet-lease program, shifted all United Kingdom flights to its own Boeing 777 planes, claiming Norse announced the suspension with no notice as PIA passengers were preparing to board.

Norse, amid rising fuel costs from the Iran war, began leasing out its Boeing 787 fleet to other airlines as it struggled to make a profit on trans-Atlantic flights. In July, IndiGo, India's largest carrier, announced it would conclude its own wet-lease program with Norse by the end of October.

Norse's stock price plummeted and closed down 85%. Most of its value has been wiped out since the start of the year and the stock is now trading at $0.010.

Jet fuel prices in Europe have more than doubled since March amid fallout from the Iran war and the restrictions on oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz, where up to 20% of the world's petroleum flowed before the onset of the war in February.

The price increases have forced other airlines, most notably budget carrier Spirit Airlines, to shut down as well.

DUFFY BLAMES BIDEN-BUTTIGIEG TEAM FOR SPIRIT AIRLINES COLLAPSE AFTER BLOCKED MERGER

"Long-haul, low-cost is most exposed to high fuel costs as demand is subject to a high level of price elasticity. So maybe not a surprise," aviation analyst James Halstead told Reuters.

Norse Atlantic did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Your holiday shopping data needs a cleanup before Black Friday
item.description: Data brokers may expose your name, home address and phone number to scammers sending fake USPS delivery texts ahead of the Black Friday shopping rush.
item.content:encoded:
Your phone buzzes: "USPS: Your package could not be delivered due to an incomplete address. Update your details within 12 hours." You did order something last week. Probably several things. So your thumb hovers over the link. That's the whole trick.

Black Friday lands on Nov. 27 this year, and the holiday delivery rush is already underway. That gives scammers plenty of opportunities to send fake delivery alerts that arrive when you're expecting a package.

Meanwhile, your shopping habits and personal details may be circulating through data brokers. Here's how that information can make scams more convincing and what you can do to clean it up before the holiday shopping rush gets even busier.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

A SCAMMER HAS YOUR NAME, PHONE NUMBER AND ADDRESS. WHAT CAN THEY ACTUALLY DO?

Every time you shop online, sign up for a discount or share your contact information, you may add to a growing collection of personal data. Some businesses use that information for their own marketing, while others share certain details with advertising partners or data brokers.

Here's where some of that information comes from:

As I've covered before, loyalty programs and store memberships can contribute to the information companies collect about you. Add the personal details available through people-search sites, and someone looking to target you may find more information than you'd expect. The FTC explains that people-search companies collect information from multiple sources and sell reports containing personal details, sometimes including relatives' names and addresses.

You can use the free exposure scanner we recommend at CyberGuy.com to check whether your personal information appears on publicly searchable websites. Keep in mind that a free scan cannot uncover every private data broker database. The results might surprise you.

WHY CAREFUL PEOPLE STILL END UP ON DATA BROKER SITES

A fake delivery text doesn't need to know exactly what you ordered. During the holidays, plenty of people are expecting packages, so a message about a delivery problem can seem believable. Scammers often send these messages to large numbers of phone numbers without knowing anything about the recipients. However, personal information obtained from public sources or data brokers can help make some scams more convincing.

Here's how that information could be misused:

The FTC reported that fake package delivery problems, often involving messages impersonating USPS, were the most commonly reported type of text scam in 2024. The problem extends beyond package deliveries. According to FTC testimony released in March 2026, Americans reported $15.9 billion in fraud losses during 2025 across all scam categories. A typical fake delivery message directs you to a convincing website and asks you to pay a small redelivery fee. That payment request is the trap. The scammer wants your credit card details and may also try to collect other sensitive information. Here's something important to remember: USPS does not charge a fee for redelivery. Its legitimate text tracking service also requires you to request tracking information first, and those tracking messages do not contain links.

Data removal takes time. Brokers process opt-out requests on different schedules, and personal information can reappear even after it has been removed. Starting now gives you a chance to identify exposed information and begin requesting removals before the busiest shopping days arrive.

There is one important distinction. Removing your information from data brokers can reduce your exposure over time, but it cannot guarantee that scam texts will stop or prevent scammers from contacting you this holiday season. That's why data cleanup should go hand in hand with safer shopping and delivery habits.

You can get started in about 15 minutes, although completing data removal requests and having companies process them can take much longer.

Look up your name on people-search websites such as Spokeo, Whitepages or BeenVerified. Check whether your home address, phone number or relatives' information appears. If you find information you want removed, look for the site's opt-out instructions.

Check the privacy settings on the websites and apps you use most frequently. Look for options to limit promotional emails, personalized advertising and sharing with marketing partners. You can also review saved shipping addresses and remove outdated entries you no longer need. Keep in mind that deleting a saved address may not erase information retained in previous order records.

If a message claims there's a delivery problem, open the retailer's or shipping company's official app or website yourself. Check the tracking number and delivery status there. Do not enter payment details through a link in an unsolicited message, even if it includes your name or address.

Instead of spending hours submitting individual opt-out forms, an automated data removal service can send removal requests to hundreds of data brokers, depending on the provider and plan you choose. Some services also submit recurring removal requests to help address information that reappears. While no service can erase every piece of information about you online, it can help reduce your exposure. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

Talk with your parents and other relatives about fake delivery messages. Make sure everyone knows to verify unexpected payment requests through the carrier's official website or app. For USPS specifically, explain that it does not charge redelivery fees. A message demanding immediate payment to release a package should raise suspicion.

If you receive a suspicious delivery message, don't respond or click the link. You can forward scam texts to 7726 (SPAM) and use your phone's reporting feature. For messages impersonating USPS, you can also report them to spam@uspis.gov. If you already entered your credit card information on a suspicious website, contact your card issuer immediately. Ask about blocking the card, disputing fraudulent charges and monitoring your account for unauthorized activity. You can also report the incident at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

What concerns me most about these fake delivery texts is how easily they blend into our holiday routines. When you're ordering gifts and waiting for packages, a message about a delivery problem can catch you at exactly the wrong moment. I also think we need to pay more attention to how much personal information is floating around online. Taking a few minutes to search your name, review your shopping accounts and start removing exposed information is worthwhile. But remember, even if you clean up your data, scammers can still reach you. My advice is simple: Never let an unexpected text dictate how you check on a package. Open the official app or website yourself and verify what's actually happening before you share a single detail.

Have you received a fake package delivery text that looked convincing, and how did you figure out it was a scam? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

item.title: Trump, NATO chief push Russia to avoid any actions that would 'expand the war' with Ukraine
item.description: President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte, who met Wednesday night at Mar-a-Lago, urged Russia to avoid actions that might expand the Ukraine war.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte are calling on Russia to avoid making any moves "that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war" against Ukraine.

The declaration came after the pair got together at Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thanksgiving Eve for what was described as an "outstanding meeting."

However, Russia hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight, according to the mayor of the Ukrainian capital.

"The meeting was very impactful, with the war between Russia and Ukraine and the conflict in Iran being the primary subjects, as well as all of the record setting achievements that we have made together at the summits in the Hague and at Ankara," Trump and Rutte said in a joint statement.

"We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible," the statement added. "Lastly, we talked about the importance of continuing to expand defense spending and investment in our industrial base, both in the United States and across NATO."

PUTIN'S WAR DEATH TOLL REPORTEDLY TOPS 700,000 AS RUSSIA SCRAMBLES FOR RECRUITS

Rutte said in a post on X following the meeting, "It’s clearer than ever that American leadership remains essential as we build a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO."

The Kremlin on Thursday accused Ukraine of trying to expand the war after Ukraine sank a Russian warship in Libya using drones and attacked a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland this past weekend, Reuters reported.

"As regards the escalation of the conflict in Ukraine, this appears to refer to attempts by the Kyiv regime to expand the geographical scope of this conflict. We are witnessing terrorist activity by the Kyiv regime in the Mediterranean and the Baltic," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov was quoted as saying.

NATO SECRETARY GENERAL MARK RUTTE WARNS ON UKRAINE WAR RISKS AHEAD OF TRUMP MEETING

"This cannot fail to cause concern amongst coastal states, and most likely within the Alliance as a whole — the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. Of course, nobody would want the conflict to spread geographically, and these are potentially very dangerous actions on the part of the Kyiv regime," Peskov added, according to Reuters.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said at least seven people were wounded in Russian strikes overnight, hitting a shopping center and other buildings, Reuters also reported.

Russia's Defense Ministry reportedly claimed that it struck two sites linked to the production of drones.

item.title: Parents of potential first Gen Z saint share daughter's powerful final message of hope
item.description: Maria Middleton's parents recall her words after a terminal brain tumor diagnosis as bishops advance her cause to become the first Gen Z saint.
item.content:encoded:
The parents of a Doylestown, Pennsylvania, teenager who could become the Catholic Church's first Gen Z saint are sharing their daughter's powerful message of hope, recalling how she remained steadfast in her faith while braving a terminal brain tumor diagnosis.

"I will not despair. I will choose hope," Maria Middleton told her parents just two weeks after her diagnosis.

Her father, Brian Middleton, recounted the conversation Tuesday on "The Story with Martha MacCallum." Brian, along with his wife, Susan, joined the show to reflect on their daughter's legacy and the movement to canonize her as a saint.

GEN Z FLOCKING TO CATHOLIC CHURCHES IN NYC FOR YOUTH GROUPS, SOCIAL EVENTS AMID CONVERSION BOOM

"Maria made a decision that she wasn't going to cling to life, that she was going to spend it in self-transcendent service to others," Brian said, recalling his daughter's determination to not let her diagnosis define her remaining time.

"Two weeks after she was diagnosed, we asked her how she was doing. And she said, 'Mom and Dad, regardless of the circumstances of my life, my mission and purpose remain the same, and it's to know, love and serve God... my emotions will rise and fall, but my faith is not an emotion. It's a commitment and I will not despair. I will choose hope,'" he added.

"Her faith was so well integrated into her life that her decisions were always based on what was good, what was true, what was beautiful," Susan chimed in.

"That's how Maria navigated through life, always going back and saying to herself, and we found this in her journal... 'Only what God thinks matters.'"

FULTON SHEEN BECAME A TV SENSATION PREACHING FAITH, MORALITY AND WARNINGS MICHAEL KNOWLES SAYS STILL RESONATE

Maria died in 2020 at just 18 years old, approximately 20 months after being diagnosed with an inoperable brain tumor. Her commitment to faith and serving others has since drawn widespread attention, prompting Catholic leaders to take a preliminary step toward her possible canonization.

On Nov. 17, the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops voted to advance Middleton's cause for canonization, marking an early step in a process that could eventually see her recognized as the Catholic Church's first Gen Z saint.

The move comes a little over one year after Pope Leo canonized the first millennial saint, St. Carlo Acutis.

For her parents, the growing movement to recognize Maria as a saint reflects the lasting impact of her message, which they say continues to resonate with people around the world.

"In this world of despair, she's become a patroness of hope because of the way that she lived her life. In this world with anxiety, suicide, and depression, Maria made a decision that she was going to live out her life on a daily basis. She chose gratitude over anger," Brian said.

"And because of this international movement, it's come to the attention of the Archdiocese of Philadelphia, and they're seeing that Maria appears to have lived a life of heroic virtue, and we trust that the church will do a good job."

"But the thing that's undeniable is the impact that Maria has had on so many lives around the world... in this age of despair, she's a light of hope."

item.title: A look at how the Trumps spend their Thanksgiving holiday through the years
item.description: Donald Trump marks his sixth Thanksgiving as president with the White House turkey pardon, after past holidays at Mar-a-Lago and Bagram Airfield.
item.content:encoded:
In keeping with tradition, President Donald Trump marked his sixth Thanksgiving in the executive office with the White House’s annual Turkey Pardon ceremony on Tuesday.

His plans for Thanksgiving Day this year remain unannounced — but previous holidays offer a preview of how the president likes to spend the day honoring those who can't be at home for the uniquely American holiday due to service to the country.

Last year, Trump spent Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago participating in his favorite pastime — golf. But he also used the time in what is known as the "Winter White House" to call Maj. Gen. Dave Gardner, commander of the 101st Airborne Division and Joint Task Force–Southern Border, by video conference and talk with troops deployed along the southern border.

TRUMP AND DANA WHITE HONOR MARINE CORPS BAND WITH SIX-FIGURE CHECKS IN FIRST EVENT ON NEW HELIPAD

First lady Melania Trump spent the days ahead of the holiday in 2025 visiting Camp Lejeune and Marine Corps Air Station New River with second lady Usha Vance on Nov. 19. They met with military families and made Thanksgiving crafts with children.

In 2020, during the final Thanksgiving of his first term, Trump remained at the White House and made calls to six deployed military units representing every branch of the armed forces, including troops in Kuwait and sailors aboard the USS Winston Churchill in the Red Sea.

Trump famously took a secret trip to Bagram Airfield in Afghanistan on Nov. 28, 2019, where he served turkey, posed for photos and thanked American troops for their sacrifices amid the ongoing war in the Middle East, which not even two years later, in August 2021, was brought to an end by then-President Joe Biden.

"There's nowhere I'd rather celebrate this Thanksgiving than right here with the toughest, strongest, best, and bravest warriors on the face of the Earth," Trump told the troops at the time.

"And you don't even know how much the people of our country love and respect you."

TRUMP SAYS US MAY RECOVER ALL THE EQUIPMENT LEFT BEHIND IN AFGHANISTAN BY BIDEN ADMIN

The visit came as roughly 12,000 American troops remained in Afghanistan more than 18 years after the U.S. invasion.

During the visit, Trump met with Afghan President Ashraf Ghani to discuss efforts to end the war and told American troops that the Taliban wanted to reach a deal with the United States. He said his administration was reducing America's military presence in Afghanistan while pursuing a political solution to the more than 18-year conflict.

Trump spent Thanksgiving 2018 in Florida having a traditional dinner with his family, including Melania and his children and grandchildren.

He also held a video call with deployed troops before visiting Coast Guard members at Station Lake Worth Inlet with his wife, where the first couple thanked them for their service and hurricane rescues.

After that holiday in 2018, Melania and then-second lady Karen Pence assembled comfort kits for deployed troops at American Red Cross headquarters.

Trump spent his first Thanksgiving as president at his Mar-a-Lago estate for a traditional Thanksgiving dinner with his family. It came after a day of video-calling deployed troops.

Donald and Melania Trump also visited Coast Guard Station Lake Worth Inlet in Riviera Beach, Florida, where they handed out food and greeted service members.

item.title: CFP selection committee continues to churn out inexplicable, indefensible rankings | Ian Miller
item.description: The Indiana Hoosiers dropped six spots in the College Football Playoff rankings after an overtime loss to Washington, while Alabama fell just three.
item.content:encoded:
The College Football Playoff selection committee released its updated rankings Tuesday evening to, well, less controversy than a typical week.

There was movement near the top of the rankings, thanks to the UCLA Bruins suffering their first loss of the season in triple overtime at Michigan and the Indiana Hoosiers falling in overtime to the Washington Huskies in Seattle. Then there's the Tennessee Volunteers-Alabama Crimson Tide debate, which this week resulted in a long-awaited changing of the order between the two teams.

After weeks of the Crimson Tide sitting above UT, despite a head-to-head loss, the Volunteers jumped them to sit at No. 5. That might have been reasonable, considering the committee's absurd "logic," but there's plenty from this week's poll that isn't. And it's yet again a sign of how the committee just makes things up as they go.

CFP SELECTION COMMITTEE HAS OFFICIALLY DISCREDITED ITSELF WITH LATEST RANKINGS

First? How they've handled the Hoosiers this season, and particularly the last few weeks.

Just three polls ago, Indiana was ranked No. 4 by the selection committee. After not playing for a bye week, they dropped all the way to No. 9. That was bizarre enough, considering again, they didn't play. The committee's excuse for this was that all of the Hoosiers' Big Ten opponents lost in the same week, devaluing their strength of schedule. We'll come back to that.

After the bye week, Indiana beat the then-No. 18 team, the USC Trojans, at home by two scores. It moved up just one spot to No. 8. Ahead of this week's poll, the Hoosiers lost on the road to overtime to a team now ranked in the selection committee's own poll. They dropped six spots. Six. So it didn't play, beat a top-15 team by two scores, lost on the road in overtime to a ranked team, and dropped from No. 4 to No. 14. This would never happen to a team from say, another conference that enjoys enhanced protection from consequences.

When the Georgia Bulldogs lost, at home, to an unranked Auburn team, they dropped four spots in the AP Top 25. Yes, the AP poll uses a different set of voters, but it's indicative of the different standards applied to different conferences.

BIG TEN FACES ONE-BID NIGHTMARE IN CFP RANKINGS AS SEC EYES FOUR BIDS AND BIG 12 COULD THRIVE

What makes the Indiana ranking even more, shall we say, confusing, is how it compares to say, Alabama. The committee had a golden opportunity to keep their standards consistent when all of Alabama's SEC wins lost in the same week between the second and third polls. Had they applied the same logic to the Tide as they did with Indiana, they'd have dropped multiple spots. They didn't move at all.

This week presented another opportunity for consistency. All of Alabama's SEC wins lost again, except for Mississippi State who beat FCS Tennessee Tech 34-16, which may or may not have counted as a Quality SEC Win™. Alabama dropped just three spots. They're now No. 6, while the Hoosiers are eight places behind them at No. 14. With the same record.

Now, there are multiple ways to evaluate records, strength of schedule and overall resume. But the committee seemingly prioritizes how teams perform against their own rankings. This is a terrible idea that inevitably creates circuitous logic, but it's how they've chosen to operate. Ok, fine.

Taking them at their word, here's how Alabama has done against teams currently ranked in the CFB playoff top-25:

That's it. This is the strength of schedule that boosts the Tide's resume, in the committee's mind, to worthy of being eight spots ahead of Indiana with the same record. Surely though, Indiana must have played an easy schedule that justifies such a lower spot in the poll...right?

Well, for comparison, here's how the Hoosiers have done against currently ranked teams:

So they've played two more games against ranked opponents, and what do you know? They actually won two of those games! Their two losses have come by a combined seven points, including one to a top-5 quality Ohio State team with its starting quarterback healthy. That came down to one of the last plays of the game.

We can also look at ESPN's SP+ to point out how absurd the disparity is. While the perception is that Indiana's played an easy schedule, because of its non-conference opponents, nobody makes that claim about the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs. Even though Georgia, by an objective analytics-driven measurement, has played an easier schedule than Indiana. And a similarly week non-conference slate.

Here's how the two schedules compare in SP+ rankings:

Indiana

Georgia

Interesting. Also per SP+, Indiana's schedule ranks as the 38th hardest in the country. Georgia is 44th. Alabama is 14th, so harder than the Hoosiers, but again, they have the same record. The difference does not justify an eight spot differential. Heck, Miami's played a tougher schedule than Georgia, yet they somehow sit at No. 7 in the poll behind not one, not two, but three two-loss SEC teams. Despite the same number of losses, and its one loss coming down to a controversial incomplete pass call late in the fourth quarter on the road to a top-5 team. Not Auburn.

In fact, speaking of SEC teams getting the benefit of the doubt, Tennessee's strength of schedule is just 22nd, and they're 1-1 against teams currently ranked in the top-25. Their non-conference schedule, like Georgia's and Indiana's, is embarrassingly bad. They beat up on Furman 56-9, the same awful Georgia Tech team 45-24, and Kennesaw State 42-9. Its loss to South Carolina looks worse than Indiana's two losses now, and they have fewer wins over ranked teams. Why is it nine spots ahead of Indiana with a relatively comparable schedule?

The answer, as always, is perception. And selection committee chair Hunter Yurachek confirmed that in his typically embarrassing post-poll interview. When asked why the switch between Tennessee and Alabama, Yurachek basically said the committee just felt like it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"When we first ranked Alabama at No. 3 two weeks ago, the resume looked different than it did when we started the ranking process this week. So much so that the committee felt that both Texas and Notre Dame deserved to be ranked ahead of Alabama," he told Rece Davis. "And then you couple that with a UCLA loss, and the Indiana loss, and then a Tennessee win against LSU, Tennessee moves up to a point where they’re now directly comparable to Alabama. You got the head-to-head, Tennessee over Alabama. And that’s the switch where you have Texas at 3 now, Notre Dame at 4, Tennessee at 5, and Alabama at 6."

Why does beating an unranked 6-5 LSU team make Tennessee comparable to Alabama? What has Alabama actually accomplished besides losing its two toughest games of the year?

When asked about Indiana, he gave an even more rambling and incoherent answer.

"For the last six weeks, Indiana's had six one-score games. Three out of the last four have been in overtime. And until Saturday, they had found a way to win those games," he said.

This is wrong. Indiana beat USC 27-13 roughly 10 days ago. Does the committee not know the outcomes of the games? Because that is factually incorrect. Unfortunately for America, he wasn't done there.

"But Saturday, they did not," he continued. "They fell behind the team like a Texas Tech with one loss and then they were in direct comparison with their counterparts in the Big 10 in Oregon and Iowa. You got both of those teams. Oregon has won four games in a row. Iowa has also won four games in a row. Oregon has a win at Ohio State. Iowa lost at home to Ohio State."

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Why was Indiana only in direct comparison to other Big Ten teams? Do the two-loss SEC teams not exist? Or is the committee so hopelessly inept and biased that they think two-loss Alabama and Tennessee simply can't be compared to the Big Ten because they're in the mighty SEC and play in big stadiums or something? Four of Indiana's last six games have been against teams currently ranked in the top-25, so why would it be surprising they were close? Though again, it did beat USC by two scores, which Yurachek got wrong.

Does he and the committee also think beating OSU without Julian Sayin is the same as beating it with him? Because Oregon's win was after his injury, and Iowa and Indiana's losses were before the injury. Incompetence all the way down.

Or maybe they're just mad because Cignetti continues to call out the committee's obvious bias.

Tennessee lost one of its last four games, and their three ensuing wins have come over teams that are a combined 0-9 in their last nine. In fact, Tennessee's resume SP+ is No. 10, while Indiana is No. 11 and UCLA is No. 9. Tennessee is ranked nine spots ahead of Indiana and four spots ahead of UCLA. Guess that doesn't matter though! Cause SEC!

What these inconsistencies and illogical arguments boil down to is that the committee believes losses in the SEC shouldn't matter much. They believe that the SEC deserves preferential treatment it hasn't earned, particularly considering that conference's atrocious record in the playoff the past three seasons. There's a very real chance the Big Ten, which undoubtedly has a stronger middle class than the SEC this year, only gets one team in the tournament. While the SEC will get four. And we already know that the SEC conference championship game can't hurt the loser, a ridiculous fact Joey Galloway thankfully brought up on ESPN's show, to great consternation and disappointment from Rece Davis and Heather Dinich.

Ranked wins don't matter, objective resumes don't matter, the only thing that matters is perception. Which is why this poll will continue to be a discrediting embarrassment.

item.title: Dak Prescott's 1,000-yard, 11-touchdown surge over three games makes Cowboys heavy Thanksgiving favorites
item.description: Happy Thanksgiving! Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys already beat the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 this season ahead of their Thanksgiving rematch.
item.content:encoded:
Happy Thanksgiving to all you turkeys out there. I hope your plate is full, your turkey is moist, the stuffing is aplenty, and most of all, that we make a ton of money today. By the time this game comes on, you probably will be either about to start your dinner or heading to the in-laws for the next meal.

What could be better today? Well, a win in this game would be a bit of help, and let’s see if we can get that with the Eagles and Cowboys.

The Philadelphia Eagles were impressive on Sunday, and that’s saying something. The team has been a bit of a disaster this season, specifically with Jalen Hurts and his injury situation. They come into today’s game with a 3-7 record and are probably just trying to play spoiler for any opponent at this point in their season. They aren’t mathematically eliminated from the postseason or anything, but they might as well be. And that’s taking into consideration the win they had Sunday.

Before we go and say that Joe Milton III is the answer at quarterback, let’s just admit that the Steelers aren’t exactly a great team. They are fine, but a really bad first quarter did Pittsburgh in for the game. The Eagles only scored six points the remainder of the game, and the Steelers outscored them 16-6 from the start of the second quarter on. A win is a win, but I don’t think want anyone thinking the Eagles have figured something out.

The good news for them is that they at least put up some points against a defense that is certainly better than what Dallas has to offer.

EAGLES QB JOE MILTON SHARES THAT HE SAYS HIS DAUGHTER'S NAME TO CALM NERVES BEFORE THROWING A DEEP BALL

The Dallas Cowboys are basically just running back what they did last season. I hate to bash the team because I was pretty high on them before the season started, but their only method of victory is to have Dak Prescott go bonkers and throw for a million yards and 10 touchdowns a game.

Obviously, I’m exaggerating here, but he does have almost exactly 1,000 passing yards and 11 touchdowns over the past three games. If he had any semblance of a defense this season, he might be in the MVP conversation as I predicted before the year.

BUT… he doesn’t. His defense is awful. They are ranked near the bottom in passing and rushing yards allowed, and they are giving up a ton of points. It means Prescott has to be near perfect for them to win. Even when he was close against the 49ers, they still lost by six because the defense couldn’t give him any help. Dallas is a fun team to watch, but it has to be frustrating for true fans of the club.

COWBOYS STAR QUINNEN WILLIAMS REPEATS SIX WORD ANSWER 12 TIMES IN PRESSER AFTER MAJOR COACHING CHANGE

Prescott and the Cowboys have already beaten the Eagles once this season. They went into Philadelphia and won 38-21. I’m not really sure why they aren’t bigger favorites in this one, outside of maybe because Philly looked a bit better with Milton under center. I like the Cowboys to cover the -8.5 in this game, and I think their team total is a good look as well. Prescott has been playing great lately and has already shown he can rack up points against the Eagles' defense.

A win from Philly last week also makes me think they will stumble this week. Sometimes a bad team just wants to get a win and then rests a bit the next week. Give me the Cowboys -8.5 and give me their team total over.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen set up for another shootout as Chiefs face Bills on Thanksgiving
item.description: The Chiefs and Bills meet on Thanksgiving Day with Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen poised for an NFL shootout; the series is tied 5-5 since 2020.
item.content:encoded:
I don’t know if you know this or not, but we are at the main course of your Thanksgiving Day with this game.

Sure, you could’ve finished and might be in a food coma by the time this game kicks off, but the NFL has done a great job of giving us one game that we absolutely cannot miss late in the day. Any time the Chiefs and the Bills take each other on, it is must-see television, and that’s precisely what we get this week.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Kansas City Chiefs are one of the best teams in football again. They are coming off yet another win – a 34-7 drubbing of the Arizona Cardinals. I do think it is fair to ask if the Chiefs are actually good, or just taking advantage of an easy schedule.

Their eight wins have been over Denver, Indianapolis, Miami, Las Vegas, Los Angeles (Chargers), New York (Jets), Atlanta, and Arizona. Outside of Denver, whom they played at home and in the first week of the season, there isn’t one quality win in that group. In fact, none of those teams have winning records.

So, are the Chiefs actually good? Maybe. Patrick Mahomes has played much more like Patrick Mahomes in the past two games, throwing for 672 yards over the two games and eight touchdowns. We know he doesn’t really have a deep receiving corps, but he is making it work. I’ve harped about this for years, but Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, and Xavier Worthy are the options, and I don’t think any of them would be a true No. 1 on almost any other team.

Travis Kelce sporadically looks good, but you can’t really count on it. Kenneth Walker III is a difference-maker at running back, but he has been out the past two weeks, and they really need him to give the Bills defense something different to worry about.

The Buffalo Bills are still one of the best teams in football, and they still have their Superman, Josh Allen.

The Swiss Army Knife quarterback is arguably the best running back in football – certainly for short yardage and goal-to-go situations. He is the reason they win games, and hasn’t really been the reason for their lone loss this year. Even in the loss to the Patriots, the lone blemish on the Bills' season, he had one interception, but threw for one touchdown and ran for another. The Bills defense just couldn’t seem to stop Drake Maye – essentially the only team this season to struggle against him.

Perhaps it is worth considering if the Bills have beaten anyone this year, if I’m going to knock the Chiefs schedule. They’ve beaten Houston, Detroit, Los Angeles (both), Las Vegas, Baltimore, Minnesota, New York (Jets), and Miami. Detroit is a good team, but they got them at home.

The Rams are a solid team, but they did play them at least without Myles Garrett. The Vikings defense was still solid in their game, but got no offensive help and forced them to trade for Kirk Cousins after the game. Certainly their schedule has been harder than Kansas City’s, though.

THANKSGIVING WEEK BETTING GUIDE 2026: NFL THANKSGIVING, RIVALRY WEEK, NBA CUP, NHL AND COLLEGE HOOPS PICKS

Any time these two squads get together, you expect fireworks. Since 2020, they’ve played 10 times (including playoffs), and the series is tied 5-5, but in the regular season the Bills are 5-1 against the Chiefs. Which means … the Chiefs are 4-0 against them in the playoffs. In the ten games, the scores have been: 49, 61, 51, 51, 37, 44, 78, 58, 62, and 43. I think we'll see two quarterbacks do their thing tonight and treat us to a shootout. Give me the over 50.5.

item.title: Stone Cold Steve Austin hates slow fishing, Trey McKinney hunts geese & Steven Rinella talks turkey
item.description: Steven Rinella's wife calls skipping turkey "sinful," but the MeatEater host insists Thanksgiving dinner should feature fresh venison, elk or duck instead.
item.content:encoded:
'Field Notes' is a weekly OutKick OutDoors column featuring the biggest hunting, fishing and outdoor stories, viral videos, reader submissions and whatever else Mother Nature throws our way. It runs every Thursday on OutKick.com.

Last year, I struck a nerve with Steven Rinella.

Turns out, the MeatEater host has some very strong opinions about what belongs on the Thanksgiving dinner table. And spoiler alert: It's not turkey.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

"This … OK. This is a major issue in my marriage," Rinella told me.

You see, Rinella considers himself a Thanksgiving purist.

"I've pointed out to [my wife] that historians don't even think the Pilgrims ate turkey on the first Thanksgiving. They think they were probably eating geese or ducks," he explained. "They ate the best of what they had. They definitely ate deer meat, you know?"

So that's his philosophy. Thanksgiving dinner should be whatever you've recently harvested. Venison, elk, duck — whatever's good and fresh. His wife, Katie, on the other hand, thinks it's downright "sinful" to skip the traditional turkey.

But if you are committed to turkey, Rinella thinks you're probably cooking it wrong.

According to Steve, roasting a whole bird is one of the worst ways to prepare it. By the time the legs are cooked through, the breast is usually dried out. Or, as he put it, "incinerated."

His solution? Break the bird down and cook each part the way it deserves. Smoke the breasts, slow-cook the legs and thighs, and stop trying to make every piece of a very lean animal finish cooking at the same time.

And if you're one of those people who thinks turkey is dry, bland and generally inferior to the mashed potatoes?

"Not the turkey's fault," Rinella deadpanned.

Fair enough.

To Rinella’s horror, I’m sure, I come from a bird-in-the-oven family myself. But it was always a treat when my uncle or grandpa would bring home a harvest for the holidays. Hard to beat wild turkey on your plate and Wild Turkey in your glass.

But, I'm curious where you guys stand.

Are you taking the Rinella approach and serving up venison, elk or whatever happens to be in the freezer? Did you save a wild turkey from spring hunting season? Or are you perfectly content shoving a regular ol' Butterball in the oven and calling it a day?

No judgment! Just whatever you do, don't do this:

Send me your menus, photos and strongly held opinions at Amber.Harding@outkick.com. Bonus points if you harvested dinner yourself.

And with that, let's get into this week's Field Notes.

Stone Cold Steve Austin is retired from the ring these days. Now, he's focused on winning off-road championships and — in his downtime — hunting and fishing.

But if the fish ain't biting, Steve ain't happy.

Off the track, the late Kyle Busch was an avid hunter and outdoorsman. In fact, before his death in May, Kyle entered Maine's coveted moose permit lottery. His name was drawn in June, and his son Brexton ultimately went on the hunt in his place.

So I knew the Busch family had an appreciation for the great outdoors.

Still, nothing could have prepared me for the room in Samantha Busch's recent Instagram post.

Samantha is asking for book recommendations, but I'm going to need everyone to direct their attention to the furniture for a moment.

The chair. The antlers. The walls. That little window. Did somebody commission Fred Flintstone to design a hunting lodge?

I have — respectfully — 400 questions about this room, and not one of them is about books.

Tomorrow, it's officially time to start decorating for Christmas. If you're like me (and this buck I'm about to show you), you've already started.

Like a squirrel determined to pilfer bird seed, be ungovernable.

Horse pants! That's it. That's all I have to say.

Back in September, just days after Trey McKinney became the youngest Bassmaster Angler of the Year in history, I caught up with the 21-year-old fishing phenom on "Open Season."

And while we talked plenty about bass fishing, Trey made it very clear he had other things on his mind.

"I basically make my money fishing to spend hunting," he told me.

He explained that once tournament season wraps up, he trades his fishing rods for shotguns and spends much of the fall and winter chasing waterfowl with his buddies. It's how he unwinds after months on the road.

Well, Trey wasn't kidding.

He just shared a video of himself absolutely hammering geese with Front Range Guide Service.

The fish finally get a break, and now the birds have to deal with this guy.

Alexa, play "Good Old Dogs and God."

Someone's cutting onions in here.

This week on "Open Season," I sat down with Hannah Graham, co-founder of Marsupial Gear, to talk about her unforgettable first elk hunt in Arizona.

I really appreciated Hannah's honesty in sharing the emotional side of hunting — something that often gets overshadowed by photos of trophy bucks, a freezer full of meat and mounts on the wall.

Taking an animal's life comes with a responsibility that no good hunter takes lightly. And Hannah was refreshingly candid about the pressure, self-doubt and emotions that came with that responsibility.

It's a side of hunting we don't talk about enough, and I think it's a conversation worth having.

Check out our full interview here and don't forget to subscribe:

Let's open the mailbag.

We want to see your biggest catches, hunting harvests, outdoor adventures and whatever ridiculous thing showed up on your trail cam. Got a great story, a burning question or just something you want to get off your chest? We want that, too.

Send it all to Amber.Harding@outkick.com or tag @outkickoutdoors on Instagram for a chance to be featured in Field Notes.

Amber:

First of all, I'm always interested in pictures of beautiful sunsets. Hit me with 'em. Anytime, anywhere.

item.title: Steelers star DK Metcalf has to be 'a lot smarter' after poking opponent in the eye, NFL analyst says
item.description: DK Metcalf was ejected after poking Cooper DeJean in the face, his second personal foul, and analyst Matthew Berry said the Pittsburgh Steelers star must be smarter.
item.content:encoded:
Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy might be offering the same instructions to DK Metcalf a parent would tell their toddler: Don't poke people in the eye.

The Steelers star wide receiver was ejected in the third quarter of the team's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday for sticking a finger in the face of defensive back Cooper DeJean. It was his second personal foul of the afternoon, warranting an ejection, and NFL analyst Matthew Berry had a simple reaction to it.

"My first reaction to that is like DK's gotta be smarter than that," Berry told OutKick in a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"This is an important game and so DK's got to be a lot smarter than that. I think, and given that it's not the first incident with him, I think if I was Mike McCarthy and his Steelers teammates, I'd be really disappointed. If I was a Steelers fan, I'd be disappointed."

Metcalf denied poking DeJean in the eye.

The NFL will not be suspending Metcalf for the incident, which is fortunate for him and the Steelers. The incident with DeJean on Sunday was not a one-off for him. Since entering the NFL in 2019, he has been the most penalized wide receiver in the league.

DK METCALF'S TANTRUMS ARE HURTING HIS TEAM AS HE ACTS LIKE EVERYONE ELSE IS THE PROBLEM | MATT CALKINS

The 28-year-old has committed seven unnecessary roughness penalties, four taunting penalties, 13 holdings and 17 pass interference calls, according to The Athletic.

Berry stressed that in a competitive AFC North, and the AFC as a whole, the Steelers need Metcalf on the field.

"You're in a very tough division with the Browns and the Bengals. You're in the AFC in terms of, we just talked about the, regardless of whether we think the Chiefs are real or not," Berry, who spoke on behalf of DraftKings, said. "You got the Chiefs, you've got the Broncos, you've got the Bills, right? You've got the Jaguars. I mean, here come the Texans. So you've got nothing, nothing's guaranteed with the Steelers."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The other issue with Metcalf this season is he hasn't produced like he usually does. In 10 games, he has 36 catches for 434 yards and two touchdowns, which is on pace for a career low in yards. Berry noted that the Steelers do have other options at wide receiver and should be getting healthier.

Third-year wide receiver Roman Wilson returned this week from injury, Michael Pittman Jr. returned to practice and rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard has been solid for them this season.

Regardless of having other quality options, the Steelers need their $132 million wide receiver to step up. They are 6-4, battling for the AFC North crown, and if they fall short in that endeavor, a Wild Card spot.

However, Metcalf can only be productive if he keeps his emotions on the field. His next opportunity will be against the Denver Broncos on Friday, which they play at.

item.title: Secret Pentagon UFO hunt drew blueprints for hidden Nevada bunker to store ‘exotic’ materials
item.description: Declassified Pentagon records reveal Bigelow Aerospace planned a secret underground vault in Nevada to store recovered UAP hardware and samples.
item.content:encoded:
Buried beneath 15 to 20 feet of Nevada earth, behind 3-foot-thick reinforced concrete walls, a steel vault door and a heavily guarded access tunnel, a Pentagon contractor drew up plans to build a 5,000-square-foot subterranean fortress.

The bunker was designed to store what was described as acquired "exotic material or tissue" – including recovered hardware and biological samples tied to unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP), the Pentagon’s broader term for UFOs and other unexplained sightings in the air, space or sea.

The blueprint was not drawn from science fiction. It is detailed inside a 538-page declassified contractor report released by the Department of War as part of the Trump administration's latest batch of UAP records, exposing how close a private firm came to building a secure repository under a $22 million Pentagon program.

EX-PENTAGON OFFICIAL SAYS UAP FILES REVEAL 'TREASURE TROVE' OF INTELLIGENCE DATING BACK TO THE 1940S

The vault plans highlight the ambitions behind the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program – also referred to in Pentagon correspondence as the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program.

Launched in 2008 through a $10 million congressional earmark steered by then-Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, D-Nev., and the late Sen. Daniel Inouye, D-Hawaii, the effort was billed as a study of foreign aerospace threats out to 40 years in the future.

Internal Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) briefing notes from May 2009 say Reid was hunting for radical technological "leaps" across 12 areas – ranging from futuristic propulsion and stealth to directed-energy weapons, space-time travel and how advanced craft affect pilots.

Behind closed doors, however, contractor Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) was preparing to acquire and store physical materials.

'NON-HUMAN' BODIES ALLEGEDLY RECOVERED FROM CRASHED UFO, DOCUMENTARY FILMMAKER CLAIMS

When the DIA solicited bids in August 2008, only one company applied: North Las Vegas-based BAASS, founded by longtime Reid supporter Robert Bigelow. The DIA awarded the contract the following month.

Within weeks, BAASS moved into a nondescript building on South Polaris Avenue in Las Vegas and began turning it into a fortified compound – installing soundproofed offices, electronic deadbolts, tinted windows, security cameras and an 8-foot perimeter fence while stripping all company names and logos from the exterior.

By May 2009, as the firm's payroll swelled to 47 full-time employees – including scientists, engineers and former military and law enforcement investigators – BAASS began shopping for five additional Las Vegas Valley office buildings to house a 5,000-square-foot laboratory, physical evidence storage and a secure conference room.

At the same time, the company's administrator drew up blueprints for the underground bunker at Bigelow Aerospace's North Las Vegas complex, a site protected by razor wire, surveillance cameras and round-the-clock armed guards with military backgrounds.

UAP WHISTLEBLOWER MAKES STUNNING CLAIM ABOUT SECRETS BEHIND GOVERNMENT’S RECOVERED CRAFT

"The need for a highly secure underground vault operated by BAASS became apparent in line with a BAASS priority to pursue and acquire recovered hardware and biological samples from the corporate world and/or from private individuals and groups located elsewhere, including Brazil," the July 2009 10-month report states.

Plans called for multiple security doors along a concrete access tunnel leading into the buried structure, with any protruding surface components "extensively camouflaged," the filing adds.

To shield the program from broader scrutiny, Reid pushed the Pentagon to place the effort behind one of the military's highest secrecy walls.

On June 24, 2009, Reid wrote directly to Deputy Defense Secretary William Lynn III warning that investigators had uncovered "several highly sensitive, unconventional aerospace-related findings" that required "extraordinary protection."

Reid argued that standard classification protocols were not enough, warning that foreign intelligence services would target the program's methods and that public disclosure could scare off private industry partners.

He urged Lynn to place portions of the effort inside a Restricted Special Access Program governed by a strict "Bigoted Access List" – a tightly controlled roster limiting knowledge of the program's existence to a handful of pre-approved officials.

PENTAGON’S NEW UFO FILE RELEASE LOGS NEAR-MISS AS ‘SUPER-HEATED’ ORBS APPROACH US HELICOPTER

In an attachment to his letter, Reid proposed a 14-person access list that included himself, Inouye, Lynn, Senate aide Robert T. Herbert, seven government and military personnel and three BAASS contractors.

When DIA officials evaluated the program's actual work, however, they reached a sharply different conclusion.

In its first year, BAASS paid outside scientists to write 26 research papers on sci-fi-sounding concepts – including warp drives, wormholes, antigravity, invisibility cloaking and mind-controlled machines, contract records show.

While a DIA office initially praised the papers as solid academic surveys – noting several received positive peer reviews, including from researchers at Sandia National Laboratories – the agency's leadership refused to lock the program behind top-secret classification rules.

In a Nov. 13, 2009, memo, DIA Deputy Director Letitia A. Long formally rejected Reid's secrecy request.

"All program documents delivered to [the Defense Warning Office] during FY 2009 (the first year of the program) were unclassified because the contractor had not established a secure facility, and program employees were being vetted for clearances," Long wrote.

Later that same month, DIA Director Lt. Gen. Ronald L. Burgess Jr. and Lynn met with Reid in person and told him the contractor's reports were of "limited value to DIA," recommending the project be moved out of the intelligence agency altogether, Burgess later wrote in a December 2010 memo.

Although Congress tacked on another $12 million for the effort in fiscal year 2010 – bringing total funding to $22 million and yielding 12 additional technical reports – the DIA did not continue the contract beyond its second year.

Alongside the paper trail, the Pentagon's eighth UAP release under the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE) also included three newly declassified infrared and electro-optical sensor videos submitted by U.S. Central Command to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO).

Recorded aboard U.S. military platforms in 2020, 2023 and 2026, the clips show sensors panning and zooming to track unidentified "areas of contrast" across the frame, including a 54-second 2026 recording in which a sensor tracks two separate objects before intermittently losing contact.

item.title: 7 iconic Thanksgiving dishes Americans love to hate but keep serving every year
item.description: Every Thanksgiving table has a divisive dish, a chef says. From canned cranberry sauce to green bean casserole, here are seven that families keep serving.
item.content:encoded:
Every Thanksgiving table has a dish that seems to divide the room.

From casseroles to questionable "salads," some holiday fixtures inspire heated reactions — but still end up on the table year after year.

"Thanksgiving dishes can bring out strong opinions because they're tied to what people grew up eating," Dennis Littley, a New Jersey-based chef and founder of Ask Chef Dennis, told Fox News Digital.

FROM FONDUE TO CASSEROLES: CLASSIC 1960S FOODS THAT DEFINED A GENERATION

Some guests love them, Littley said, while others would rather pass. 

"Families keep serving these dishes because they’re part of the holiday for them," he said. "A beloved family recipe doesn't have to be everyone's favorite to earn a place on the table."

Below are seven Thanksgiving dishes that everyone loves to hate — and why families keep serving them anyway.

Cranberry grower Marcus L. Urann began commercially canning cranberry sauce in Massachusetts in 1912, and Ocean Spray, founded in 1930, later helped make it a Thanksgiving staple, according to the company's website.

DOLLY PARTON'S FAVORITE SOUTHERN DISHES, FROM CHICKEN AND DUMPLINGS TO BANANA PUDDING

While no table is complete without it, fresh and whole-berry alternatives have since entered the space, and the canned version has some harsh critics.

In a Reddit thread asking for people's opinions on the "absolutely worst and disgusting side dishes," one person cited "that cranberry gel stuff."

The sweetness and texture of dishes like cranberry sauce can be "especially polarizing," Littley said.

Campbell's recipe developer Dorcas Reilly created green bean casserole in 1955 as an easy dish made with staples like green beans and condensed cream of mushroom soup, and it gradually became a Thanksgiving fixture, Littley said.

CAMPBELL'S ROLLS OUT NEW SOUPS, INCLUDING FIRST-EVER GLUTEN-FREE CHICKEN NOODLE VARIETY

People online are divided over the dish. 

One Reddit user summed it up as "slimy canned green beans, canned 'onions' and over-salty canned soup."

While some roast the dish, others defend it.

"I love green bean casserole, but the slander every holiday season cracks me up," one person said. "I can see why it would gross people out, though."

Jell-O salads have seen a revival in the food world recently, with home cooks sharing retro molds online and chefs bringing savory aspics — meat, seafood, eggs or vegetables suspended in a gelatinous broth or consommé — back to restaurant menus, as Fox News Digital previously reported.

CLASSIC AMERICAN PANTRY STAPLES ARE GETTING A MAJOR PROTEIN- AND FIBER-PACKED MAKEOVER

Jell-O salads still find a place at some family gatherings, too, with some Reddit users describing versions with iceberg lettuce and pimento-stuffed olives, as well as cottage cheese, cheddar, walnuts and raisins.

One commenter's mother defends her lime Jell-O salad as "refreshing," while another described their family's marshmallow-and-grape version as "terrifying."

At many Thanksgiving tables is ambrosia salad, Jell-O salad's even sweeter fruit-filled cousin, usually made with canned pineapple, mandarin oranges, marshmallows and whipped topping.

"Someone keeps making ambrosia for some reason," one Redditor said of their family's holiday table. "No one touches it but it’s always there."

7 COSTCO THANKSGIVING FOOD DEALS AND STEALS THAT SHOPPERS CAN’T MISS THIS HOLIDAY SEASON

Ambrosia salad was once considered a symbol of luxury on Thanksgiving tables in the 1800s and early 1900s, according to Chowhound.

Though it has since fallen out of fashion, it remains a nostalgic Southern favorite and still has some fans. 

"I love it! But the rest of my family won’t even go near it," one internet user said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

This year, ambrosia salad is also seeing a nostalgic revival as home cooks revisit vintage potluck dishes, sometimes updating it with fresh fruit, real whipped cream or Greek yogurt.

Once considered a "poor man's" vegetable, turnips have a reputation of being bitter if overcooked.

One Reddit user said their mom mashes turnips with rutabagas every year. 

"It's just gross and funky, and she spends so much time every year trying to convince everyone else to 'just try it!'" 

Finally, last year, the family convinced her not to make it, the person said. 

"I can't tell you how much I'm looking forward to not being pressured into putting it on my plate this year."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

But not everyone has written the turnip off. 

"My aunt made a mashed turnip dish that we expected to be gross because it looked gross," one Redditor recalled. "But it surprisingly wasn’t."

For Littley, the divisive dish at his family's Thanksgiving table serves a dual purpose.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Our Thanksgiving meal has a tradition that may surprise people: We serve coleslaw," he said. "It may be regional, but we love it with the turkey dinner."

"It’s especially good on leftover turkey sandwiches with stuffing and cranberry sauce," he noted.

This dish began as a marketing idea in 1917.

The Angelus Marshmallow Company hired recipe developer Janet McKenzie Hill to create dishes featuring marshmallows, according to Smithsonian Magazine.

For some diners, the sweet-on-sweet combination is what makes the candy-coated casserole hard to stomach.

"My yuck is the classic sweet potato with marshmallows casserole," one Redditor said. "I love sweet potatoes and yams.... I like toasted marshmallows. Together they are yucky."

But the commenter summed up the Thanksgiving table standoff: "One person's yum is another person's yuck."

item.title: Where does Aaron Rodgers’ interview with Pat McAfee rank among the wildest in sports history?
item.description: Watching Aaron Rodgers bury his own coach on Pat McAfee’s show got us thinking about the wildest interviews in sports, from Richard Sherman to Mike Tyson to Jim Everett.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Rodgers went on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday and said he found out from his tight end, Pat Freiermuth, that the Steelers were benching him. It seemed like a pretty newsworthy nugget that would lead sports talk shows for the next few days.

It wasn't even close to the most interesting thing Rodgers said in the interview. Probably not even in the top five.

Rodgers accused head coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep and snoring in meetings, alleged that McCarthy led a "1-2-3 PACKERS!" cheer at halftime of Sunday's loss to the Eagles, said he’d told his head coach to give up play-calling or release him, and claimed that he joked with GM Omar Khan about McCarthy's sleeping habits.

Basically, if Rodgers was going down, he was taking McCarthy with him.

The interview went so far off the rails that, within an hour, reports surfaced that Pittsburgh was waiving Rodgers. The Steelers made it official later Wednesday afternoon. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Pittsburgh had planned to keep him on the roster before he went on the air (which made sense to me, if only to keep him away from an AFC rival).

STEELERS OFFICIALLY RELEASE AARON RODGERS AND KEEP COACH MIKE MCCARTHY ON THE JOB DESPITE EMBARRASSING CLAIMS

I honestly couldn't believe what I was watching. I’ve seen guys hurt their chances of getting another job on the way out the door, but I’ve never seen a future Hall of Fame quarterback go on national TV to bury a head coach he personally vouched for and drag his own GM into it for good measure. Imagine being the next NFL coach who has to decide whether he wants Aaron Rodgers in his building.

The closest comparison I can come up with is soccer legend Cristiano Ronaldo telling Piers Morgan he felt betrayed by Manchester United while he still played for Manchester United. The club and Ronaldo parted ways shortly thereafter. But that’s European soccer, so it doesn’t count.

Let's talk about real sports and figure out which interviews belong in the conversation with Rodgers. First, a ground rule: news conferences are out. Once you open that door, the Bears are who Denny Green thought they were, Allen Iverson is talking about practice, Jim Mora wants to know why the hell you’re asking him about the PLAYOFFS?! And Mike Gundy is a man. He’s 40.

Actually, Mike Gundy turns 60 next summer. How the hell was that almost 20 years ago?

I’m willing to grade postgame interviews on a curve because the adrenaline is pumping. One that jumps to mind is former Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman talking to Erin Andrews after the NFC Championship Game in January 2014.

Sherman had just tipped a Colin Kaepernick pass intended for Michael Crabtree into the hands of Malcolm Smith to send the Seahawks to the Super Bowl. Give me that play and a microphone, in that order, and I make no promises about what comes out of my mouth, either.

Andrews asked Sherman the standard question in that situation.

"The final play. Take me through it."

Within seconds, Sherman had declared himself the best corner in the game, called Crabtree a "sorry receiver" and warned, "Don’t you ever talk about me!"

"Who was talking about you?" Andrews asked.

"Crabtree!"

Poor Malcolm Smith. He caught the ball that sent Seattle to the Super Bowl, and thanks to Sherman, we only remember who didn’t catch it.

"Crabtree!"

Mike Tyson had 38 seconds of work under his belt when Jim Gray caught up with him in Glasgow in 2000. Gray wanted to know if that was the shortest fight of his career, which was a reasonable thing to ask a guy who’d just knocked out Lou Savarese in the amount of time it takes to melt half a stick of butter in a microwave.

Tyson wasn’t interested in looking back at what had just happened. He had a message for Lennox Lewis.

"I want to eat his children."

There's no good way to segue from Mike Tyson into anything else, but I'm a pro, so I'm going to try.

We go from eating children to an offer to (maybe) make some babies. (See? Total pro.)

Legendary NFL quarterback Joe Namath found himself with a microphone in his face on the sidelines during a 2003 Jets game, a quarter-century after he retired. On the other end of that microphone was ESPN NFL reporter Suzy Kolber.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

To start, Namath gave a perfectly normal answer about Chad Pennington. Then Kolber asked what it meant to him to see the Jets struggling.

"I want to kiss you," Namath told her before adding, "I couldn't care less about the team struggling."

The Pro Football Hall of Famer actually got back to football long enough to point out that the Jets had struggled while Pennington was out. Then, in the very same answer, he circled back to what was really on his mind.

"I want to kiss you."

To her credit, Kolber handled it with class and professionalism and simply responded, "Thanks, Joe. I'll take that as a huge compliment."

Namath later apologized to Kolber and admitted that he had been drinking for hours prior to the interview.

This is why Rodgers moves up the board for me. He chose to go on McAfee's show after finding out about his benching. Presumably, he had some time to think about what he might say. Bill Belichick had that same advantage when he sat down with CBS last year. He also had Jordon Hudson just outside the frame, which came in handy in case somebody tried to slip a tough question past him, like how the then-73-year-old football coach met his 24-year-old girlfriend.

We’re not counting that one, though, because the best answer of the entire interview came from Hudson, even though the interview subject was Belichick.

Bob Knight, on the other hand, was perfectly capable of making an interview uncomfortable all by himself. After Indiana fired him in 2000, Knight sat down with ESPN’s Jeremy Schaap to tell his side on live television.

Schaap tried to get a question in, the two started arguing about who kept interrupting whom, and Knight offered a little career advice to the son of legendary sportswriter Dick Schaap.

"You got a long way to go to be as good as your dad," Knight told him. "You better keep that in mind."

Years later, Schaap said ESPN producer Willie Weinbaum had warned him before the interview that Knight would bring up his dad to try to throw him off.

I used to produce Jeremy's ESPN Radio show, "The Sporting Life." If I’d been in Willie’s chair that day, I know exactly what I’d have said in Jeremy’s ear.

"Told ya so."

Remember Jim Gray from like 10 paragraphs ago? Ten years after Tyson, Gray was sitting across from LeBron James at a Boys & Girls Club in Greenwich, Connecticut. Millions of people wanted the answer to exactly one question. Before they got it, Gray asked LeBron if he was still biting his nails.

There was plenty of time for non-basketball questions since ESPN had set aside an hour for "The Decision."

LeBron eventually let Cleveland know he was taking his talents to South Beach. The special raised more than $2 million for the Boys & Girls Clubs, so I’ll give him credit for that. The interview itself wasn’t especially crazy. What’s crazy is that a guy wrote into Bill Simmons’ mailbag suggesting LeBron announce his decision on TV, and seven months later, millions of people were waiting for Jim Gray to get past the fingernails.

Then there’s Dennis Rodman, who went to North Korea in 2014 with a group of former NBA players to play an exhibition game for Kim Jong Un’s birthday. Take a second and read that sentence again. We haven’t even gotten to the interview.

CNN's Chris Cuomo asked whether Rodman would speak up for Kenneth Bae, an American being held in North Korea. Rodman started demanding to know whether Cuomo understood what Bae had done.

Sitting alongside him was former Knicks forward Charles Smith, left to explain that the guys were there to play basketball. Rodman later apologized to Bae’s family. Of all the people in this story, Smith might be the one I’d most like to interview. What did Dennis tell him the itinerary was?

Honorable mention for the funniest answer to an innocent question goes to Ichiro Suzuki. Bob Costas asked for his favorite American expression. Ichiro answered in English, describing August in Kansas City as "hotter than two rats in a f---ing wool sock."

Good luck asking a follow-up. Costas was laughing too hard to get one out anyway.

In 1974, ABC sat Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier down with Howard Cosell to watch their first fight ahead of their rematch. Maybe it was a simpler time, but I like to think somebody at ABC genuinely wanted to hear two guys who were about to beat the hell out of each other talk about the last time they beat the hell out of each other.

The full episode of Wide World of Sports is below. If you’re here for the fight that took place in the studio, skip to about the 56-minute mark.

The amazing part to me is that the replay had made it to the 10th round before Ali and Frazier went after each other. Try that in 2026. If those guys are still sitting in their chairs by the end of the first round, some promoter is pulling one of them aside to remind him they’ve still got tickets to sell.

Do yourself a favor and watch Cosell when they end up wrestling on the studio floor. The man stays in his chair and calls the action. I can’t say I blame him. What’s he supposed to do, get between Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier?

At least those two left the interviewer out of it. Which brings us to Jim Rome.

I never had any intention of figuring out who finished fourth or seventh on this list. I do know who finished first. In 1994, Jim Everett agreed to go on ESPN2 with Jim Rome, who’d taken to calling the quarterback "Chris," after female tennis great Chris Evert, to suggest he was afraid of getting hit.

My favorite part is when Everett starts warning Rome about calling him Chris to his face one more time, and Rome cuts in to make sure he gets credit for the first two.

"I already did it twice!"

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Everett then bet Rome he wouldn’t call him Chris again. Rome bet he would. The pause here is tremendous. Both men understand the terms. There’s still time to ask about football.

"Chris."

Everett got up and knocked Rome out of his chair. A producer stepped in, and ESPN2 cut away.

For those of you keeping score at home, Jim Rome did technically win that bet.

So where does Rodgers land? Pretty high, in my book. Sherman barely had time to take his helmet off. Rodgers had a night to sleep on it and still decided the whole country ought to know that Mike McCarthy sleeps during team meetings.

And if somebody at Thanksgiving dinner asks how you went from watching football to watching Dennis Rodman, live from North Korea, argue with Chris Cuomo, feel free to blame Aaron Rodgers.

That’s how I got here, too.

item.title: This Thanksgiving, ask yourself: What are you taking for granted?
item.description: This Thanksgiving, let's focus on gratitude for our health, employment, spouse, parents and friends we too often take for granted.
item.content:encoded:
As a young man, I started a church. I poured my life into it. I worked long hours, made big sacrifices and enjoyed every minute of it. Souls were saved, lives were changed, relationships were restored. We made a huge impact.

It was the original contemporary-style church in central Virginia. Now there are probably more than 100 such churches. It’s one of the greatest things I’ve ever done with my life. I’m so proud of all that was accomplished.

If I had to do it over, I’d do it again. In a heartbeat.

THAD ROTHROCK: BIBLE REMINDS US TO KEEP SERVING GOD EVEN AFTER WE RETIRE

But after 27 years, I left the church I founded. I did it because I felt God had more for me to do. There were many more people I could inspire. He had a larger plan for my life. I couldn’t give my full focus to the church while writing books, traveling to speak and pursuing media opportunities.

It was the right decision. I’m glad I did it.

Building facilities, expanding campuses and creating new ministries was exciting. Getting to know thousands of great folks, helping people in need and working with some fantastic, talented staff and volunteers was a joy. But it was exhausting. And with growth comes greater expectations and more entitlement.

Before you know it, people just assume there will always be powerful services, inspiring preaching, engaging children’s ministry — and that is just on Sunday. During the week, they want groups, classes and events.

It isn’t great being taken for granted. I think people thought since I started the church I would just stay for 40 years and would always be there whenever needed. It is not the reason I left. It’s the reality I experienced. You don’t serve people for recognition, but you don’t like to feel as if it’s all expected.

Thanksgiving is the one day a year we focus on gratitude for the multitude of blessings in our lives. It’s certainly good to be grateful, to take time around the Thanksgiving table and share what we are truly thankful for. But taking time each day to recall all the blessings in your life will help to keep you from taking things for granted.

DOCTOR'S 10 RULES FOR LIVING LONGER, CELEBRATING MORE BIRTHDAYS AND MAKING EXTRA YEARS COUNT

There is much we take for granted until it’s gone. Health is an obvious one. A woman in my church just sent her only child to college. She and her husband now looked forward to a new season in their lives. But instead, she was diagnosed with cancer and within months died. It’s so easy to take your health for granted until you don’t have it.

Your job is another example. Two men from my church lost their jobs and have been searching for months for employment. Highly capable and successful, they are still without employment. Having a steady income is necessary to live, and yet it’s not guaranteed. We may not love our job, but it’s better than being without one.

TIM MCGRAW WARNS OF ‘MOST DANGEROUS’ TIMES IN MARRIAGE AFTER 30 YEARS WITH FAITH HILL

And what about the people we take for granted? We could begin with our spouse. I have been traveling for years, but my wife travels less. I’ve learned that it is one thing when you are the one away from home and another when you are the one alone at home.

The times I’ve been the one at home have given me a new perspective. I have come to appreciate just how much my wife does for me. It has shown me just how much I take her for granted.

WILLIE ROBERTSON'S FAITH-BASED ADVICE THAT'S KEPT HIS 34-YEAR MARRIAGE TO WIFE KORIE STRONG

When someone is always around, you can simply take them for granted. If they are there for you, it’s so easy to think it will always be this way — until it’s not. Then you realize just how much you have taken them for granted.

Is there someone you are taking for granted? Have you considered how they make your life easier, happier, better?

THE FOUNDING FATHERS GAVE US AMERICA. 250 YEARS LATER, WE STILL DEPEND ON GOOD DADS

Maybe it’s a friend. I have a buddy I’ve known since college. He’s been such a good friend for all these years. He’s asked for so little and given so much.

Maybe you take your parents for granted. Do you appreciate all they’ve done for you over the years — their hard work that provided for you in so many ways, along with all the sacrifices they’ve made?

Maybe it’s your sibling or relative. Do you just assume they will always be there for you and will always help when you need it? It’s easy to do.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Make sure they all know how much you value them and appreciate them.

Whether it’s what you might take for granted or who you might take for granted — this Thanksgiving, be grateful for all that is in your life.

And don’t ever take it for granted.
